GC×GC is a very powerful method for analysis of aromatic compounds in low-boiling petroleum samples.

GC×GC-FPD, GC×GC-FIM and GC×GC-qTofMSD are the most powerful techniques to separate and to identify the individual BTEX compounds in low-boiling petroleum fractions, while GC×GC-FIMS and GC×GC-FPDM are the best techniques for identification and quantitation of all the C6-C11 aromatic hydrocarbon compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of reversed phase polarity capillary columns (ionic liquid and HP-5MS) is very useful for the analysis of low-boiling petroleums by GC×GC.

the application of the SLB-IL column set is an excellent choice for separation of the low-boiling petroleums and the SLB-Il111+HP-MS column combination for the comprehensive two-dimensional GC experiments.
the ionic liquid column SLB-111 is the most suitable for GC×GC analysis of aromatic hydrocarbon mixtures in low-boiling petroleum samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ionic liquid capillaries are very promising in terms of their application in the analysis of low-boiling petroleum fractions.

the use of 100% ionic liquid capillaries as a stationary phase for GC×GC-FD analysis of aromatic compounds in low boiling petroleum products provides a very powerful tool for the identification of individual aromatic compounds in these samples.

the application of ionic liquid columns in the comprehensive two dimensional gas chromatographic analysis of aromatic hydrocarbon mixtures is a powerful and promising tool for the analysis of these compounds.
